thread:
jamie: Heads-up — hitting a perf regression on speculative decode when we pair Mixtral drafts with Qwen main. Latency +15-25% and acceptance rate drops ~10%. Posting quick profiler + config. Anyone seen similar cross-family issues? :thinking:

riley: Oof. timeline? full traces?

jamie: Rooted it to model-switch path. Repro steps: 1) warm Mixtral draft (short) 2) switch to Qwen main for final token(s) 3) speculative accepts fewer proposals, more fallback regenerates. Happens under continuous batching.

jamie: Profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:03 kernel_select: chosen=gpu_fused_attention_v2 (mixtral)
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:03 kv_cache: reuse=yes, layout=packed
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:04 kernel_select: chosen=gpu_standard_attention (qwen)
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:04 kv_cache: invalidate=true -> memcpy 24MB
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:04 speculative: proposals=8 accepted=2 latency_ms=78
[profiler] 2026-03-17 14:12:04 fallback: regen_tokens=4 extra_latency_ms=40
```

jamie: Two suspects: kernel selection path forcing incompatible KV layout -> memcpy, and tokenizer mismatch reducing proposal acceptance (rope scaling/head dims matter).

nina: Do we pattern-match when switching kernels? We have a kernel compatibility table but it focuses on dtype/shape not RoPE/head metadata. Could be we don't preserve rotary base/scaling metadata across the draft->main handshake.

ryan: Noted similar before when switching between Mistral-derived and Qwen; acceptance rate dip correlated with RoPE base mismatch. Drafts compiled with rope_scale=1.0, main uses 1.05. Proposals scored wrong because rotary phase drifted.

kat: Can we short-circuit memcpy by normalizing KV layout in runtime? e.g., always use canonical packed layout and have lightweight adapters per kernel so kernel selection doesn't force global invalidate. Tradeoff: small per-kernel shim cost vs big memcpy.

jamie: I tried a quick patch to adapt layouts on the fly (kept metadata and inserted a translate kernel) — reduced memcpy but added 6-8ms per-switch. Still better than 24MB memcpy under heavy batching. Results: latency spike reduced from +25% to +7%, acceptance still low.

perf-bot: perf/regression/1902345678 attached. CI microbench shows 9% p50 increase on pairing path.

riley: For acceptance rate we should confirm tokenizer/token-id alignment. Are the draft and main using identical tokenizer versions/added tokens? Even subtle BOS/EOS differences change proposal scores.

jamie: Tokenizers match in tests. I profiled logits divergence: after switch, logits for top proposals shift ~0.6-1.2 logits on avg -> acceptance threshold misses. Suspect RoPE phase drift + head projection dimension differences (Mixtral head dim != Qwen head dim).

nina: Two actionable experiments: (A) enforce identical RoPE scaling on draft and main at handshake time (force scale to min of the two), (B) run speculative scoring in the kernel family of the main model (i.e., cast proposals to main kernel numerics before scoring) so scores are comparable. Both have tradeoffs on latency.

ryan: I can run A quickly. For B we'd need a cross-family scoring shim which might be heavy under batching. But maybe we can do it only when acceptance probability is borderline (score delta < epsilon) to save work.

kat: Also consider adaptive acceptance threshold: if we detect family mismatch or tokenizer drift increase, lower acceptance threshold slightly to keep speculative benefits. Need to monitor quality/regression.

jamie: Ran experiment A (force rope_scale=min) across 2k requests: acceptance +6%, p95 latency -4% on pairing path, but minor quality diffs on long-range dependencies (few failed coherence tests). Will iterate.

riley: Sounds promising. Can you push the test harness & results? open a draft PR and tag eng-runtime?

jamie: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 (draft). Includes profiler logs, config toggle rope_compatibility=force_min, and a small adapter kernel prototype.

nina: Cool. Next steps: 1) vet quality regressions on eval suite 2) measure batching interplay (does adapter kill batching efficiency?) 3) if ok, add a cheap fingerprint to handshake so runtime knows to apply rope_compatibility only when needed.

ryan: I'll run evals overnight and post results here. If acceptance improves without quality loss we can promote feature-flag to canary.

kat: FYI we should also add a unit that tests head/kv dim mismatches at handshake time and logs a clear event for SLO debugging. Right now it's silent.

jamie: Agree. Adding a handshake event + metrics. Thanks all. Will update PR with evals and adapter perf numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
